Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 69, verse 1–3:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Haqqah (the Inevitable Reality), because it opens with the word al-Haqqah, which is the Day of Resurrection in which the promise and the threat are realized. This word is repeated three times in the surah, to emphasize the importance of its matter.

From the aims of the surah

• Magnifying the Day of Resurrection, warning those who deny its occurrence, reminding them of the torment in this world that befell the nations who denied before them, describing the terrors of the Day of Recompense, and mentioning the state of the blessed and the wretched on that day.

• Honoring the Qur'an, the emphatic oath to the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ), and refuting the slanders of the polytheists who claimed that the Qur'an is sorcery or soothsaying, and explaining that the Qur'an is a mercy for the believers and a source of regret for the disbelievers, and implicitly containing a warning of the realization of the threat that is in the Qur'an.

[The Exegesis]

The Reality that is true, in which the promise and the threat are realized: What is the Reality that is true in its description and state? And what made you know, O Messenger, and informed you of the reality of the Resurrection, and depicted for you its terror and severity?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 69, verses 5–8:

As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the tremendous blast (al-sayha), which exceeded all bounds in its severity. As for ʿAd, they were destroyed by a cold, violently blowing wind, which Allah unleashed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, never abating and never ceasing. In those nights and days you would see the people lying dead, as if they were hollowed-out trunks of palm trees, their insides rotted away. So do you see any remnant of these people?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 69, verse 19–24:

As for the one who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, joyful and delighted: "Take, read my record! Indeed, I was certain in the world that I would meet my reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, so I prepared for it the provision of faith and righteous deeds. So he will be in a pleasant, contented life, in a lofty garden whose places and ranks are elevated. Its fruits are near, within reach of the one who stands, the one who sits, and the one who lies down. It will be said to them: 'Eat and drink with ease, free from every harm, safe from every hateful thing, because of the righteous deeds you sent forward in the past days of the world.'"
